relations.subject: data:expiration
relations.evidence: Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition lets you have documents expire after a period of time, called the document's Time To Live (TTL).

relations.subject: server:scope
relations.evidence: Scopes do not support the `maxTTL` setting.

relations.subject: data:collection-max-ttl
relations.evidence: The `maxTTL` parameter on collections and buckets sets the number of seconds a new or mutated document lasts before expiring.

relations.subject: data:bucket-max-ttl
relations.evidence: The `maxTTL` parameter on collections and buckets sets the number of seconds a new or mutated document lasts before expiring.

relations.subject: data:expiration
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate expresses a priority/override ordering between two settings; this is the answer to the brief's own question about what wins when document- and container-level expiration conflict
relations.evidence: non-zero expiration times set at a document level override a collection's non-zero `maxTTL` settings, which in turn override `maxTTL` settings at the bucket level.

relations.subject: data:collection-max-ttl
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused within this record - same mint as the relation above
relations.evidence: non-zero expiration times set at a document level override a collection's non-zero `maxTTL` settings, which in turn override `maxTTL` settings at the bucket level.

relations.subject: data:max-ttl-setting
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - the precedence rule above is a general override; this captures the specific, narrower exception stated for it: a document's OWN explicit expiration is capped, not simply overridden, by a non-zero maxTTL
relations.evidence: The `maxTTL` setting also imposes an upper limit on the expiration time you can explicitly set on an individual document in the bucket or collection.

relations.subject: data:collection-max-ttl
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - a general 'unset/zero value falls back to the containing scope's setting' shape; broader than the privilege-specific inheritsPrivilegesFrom already in the registry
relations.evidence: Setting a collection's `maxTTL` to zero does not override the bucket's `maxTTL` setting. Instead, setting the collection's `maxTTL` to zero has it inherit the `maxTTL` setting from the bucket.

relations.subject: data:max-ttl-setting
relations.evidence: When you change the `maxTTL` setting of a bucket or collection, the change does not have an immediate effect on the documents it contains.

relations.subject: data:item
relations.evidence: Couchbase Server maintains a tombstone for a period of time afterwards for each collection or item that it deletes.

relations.subject: data:metadata-purge
relations.evidence: To make sure that no trace of deleted items remain, Couchbase Server removes tombstones during a Metadata Purge.

relations.subject: data:expiry-pager
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate covers 'a background process deletes an expired entity when it runs'; firesCallback is for callback invocation, not deletion
relations.evidence: The [expiry pager](../buckets-memory-and-storage/memory.md#expiry-pager) process runs.

relations.subject: data:auto-compaction
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused within this record - same mint as the expiry-pager relation above
relations.evidence: The [auto-compaction](../../manage/manage-settings/configure-compact-settings.md) process runs.

relations.subject: server:xdcr
relations.evidence: Cross Datacenter Replication (XDCR) does not replicate the bucket or collection `maxTTL` setting from the source to the target.

relations.subject: server:xdcr
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate captures a replication mechanism copying an artifact/value to a remote target; usesProtocol/servesService describe different shapes
relations.evidence: However, by default XDCR replicates the individual document's expirations (including expirations set by the containing bucket or collection's `maxTTL` setting) to the target.

relations.subject: server:xdcr
relations.evidence: You can use [deletion filters](../../manage/manage-xdcr/filter-xdcr-replication.md#deletion-filters) to prevent XDCR from replicating expiration values.

relations.subject: server:auditing
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate states that an auditing mechanism logs changes made to a setting; excludesFromCapture is the negation of this shape, not this shape itself
relations.evidence: When you enable auditing, Couchbase Server logs changes to each bucket's `maxTTL` setting.

relations.subject: data:expiration
relations.evidence: Expiration is performed in a non-durable manner, even if a minimum level of durability is specified on the bucket.

notable_absence.finding: Document/bucket/collection expiration is gated only by edition ('Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition lets you have documents expire...') - the page never once cites a version number for when TTL, maxTTL, the precedence rules, or the exceptions were introduced, despite this being one of the oldest and most heavily used Couchbase Server features. This is the opposite failure mode from n1ql:automatic-workload-repository (dated on whats-new.md but not its own page) - here, no page anywhere in this batch supplies the missing version either, so no availableSince/evidence_source relation could be constructed even cross-page.

cross_component_finding: The already-promoted eventing:on-delete-handler is defined in the registry as 'the entry point fired on document delete/expiry' - meaning Eventing's own documentation already asserts that expiration fires OnDelete(). This expiration page, however, never mentions Eventing, OnDelete, or any handler at all: the connection exists only from the Eventing side of the registry, never stated from the data-lifecycle side. Combined with the expiry-pager/auto-compaction/query-access trigger list this page does give ('Couchbase Server deletes the document when one the following occurs: A query attempts to access it. The expiry pager process runs. The auto-compaction process runs.'), an open question for reconciliation is whether OnDelete() fires on ALL three of those triggers or only some.
cross_product_finding: This page's server:xdcr (Couchbase Server's own cross-datacenter replication mechanism, with its own maxTTL-exclusion and deletion-filter behavior) shares its name with the already-promoted capella:xdcr (recorded in the registry specifically as a monitoring-classification concept: 'a monitored Capella component ... explicitly NOT one of the Services'). Per this project's rule, that is flagged rather than merged: no page read in this batch states whether Capella's XDCR is simply Couchbase Server's XDCR running on Capella's infrastructure (which would make capella:xdcr a specialization) or something else. The same caution applies to the newly-minted server:auditing versus the already-promoted monitoring:activity-log (Capella's audit-log container) - both log administrative changes, both are called 'auditing'/'audit log' in their respective docs, and neither page states a relationship between the two products' mechanisms.
